title: Millbrook Logix integration scratchpad
content:
Meeting notes (discovery call) - Millbrook Logix - 2025-11-03

Attendees: Millbrook: Maria Reyes (CTO), Jonas Patel (Lead SRE), Anya Kovalev (Edge SW). Redwood: Priya Natarajan (solutions), Liam Chen (infra), Sofia Martinez (security).

Summary:
- Millbrook builds real-time factory edge appliances that run inference for anomaly detection and operator assistance. They want to replace a brittle cloud-dependent pipeline with a private Redwood deployment running in their on-prem datacenter and occasional regional colo.
- Primary ask: low-latency (<40ms p99 per request) inference for short sequences (max 128 tokens) with bursty traffic (spikes every 10s during shifts). Needs privacy (no cloud copy of telemetry), KMS integration, and offline-first behavior when WAN is flaky.

Key requirements (explicit):
- Deployment: Redwood Private in their VPC with an air-gapped option for certain lines.
- Models: prefer open Llama-variant family; target ~13B quantized to 4-bit (FP8/QLoRA investigations). Must support model pinning and rollback.
- Performance SLOs: 40ms p99 for single-request inference; sustain 120 RPS for batched sensor bursts across 8 devices.
- Cost/ops: limited GPU headcount (2x A100 equivalent). They want autoscaling within rack and graceful fallbacks to a smaller model variant when overloaded.
- Security: Enterprise KMS (AWS KMS + HSM on prem), audit logs, SOC2-like retention for telemetry.

Architecture constraints (from Jonas):
- VLAN + strict egress rules; outbound only to Redwood control plane on port 443 via a bastion. Intermittent outgoing window (10m/hour) for control-plane sync is acceptable.
- NUMA topology on host machines causes uneven memory availability. They prefer per-socket instance packing.
- No persistent internet for some lines (air-gapped) -> must support offline model pulls via USB/secure transfer and local registry.

Gotchas / risks called out during call:
- Quantization drift: Millbrook uses long-term accuracy for anomaly detection; 4-bit quant might change top-k distribution and increase false positives. Need eval harness on their dataset.
- KV-cache persistence: Their apps do small, repeated prompts that would benefit from persistent KV cache across restarts. Current private installer does not persist cache by default. Confirm feasibility and tradeoffs (disk encryption + crash recovery).
- Cold-starts and per-request latency: With only 2 GPUs and bursty spikes, autoscale cold-starts could violate the 40ms p99 target. Need warm pool or prefetch strategy.
- Multi-tenant packing: They have multiple production lines per rack; isolation + pinning required to avoid noisy neighbor IO.
- Model licensing & export controls for air-gapped transfer (legal will need model provenance and license checklist).

Open questions (to clarify):
- Dataset size for eval: Jonas to share representative telemetry traces (how many sequences/sec and average token length).
- Can Millbrook tolerate a small increase in false-positive rate in exchange for 2–3x cost savings? Product team must prepare quant tradeoff doc.
- Which HSM/KMS vendor (they mentioned Gemalto and AWS KMS)? Need exact KMS APIs.
- Ops window and exact firewall rules for control plane; confirm IPs + cert pinning requirements.

Immediate next steps / action items:
1) (Priya) Create a measurement plan + sample eval harness template to run their dataset against quantized 13B and 7B variants. Target due: 2025-11-10. Linked: ENG-4821.
2) (Liam) Prototype a minimal on-prem launcher that mounts a local model registry and persists KV cache to encrypted disk; test with NUMA-awareness scheduler. Due: 2025-11-17.
3) (Sofia) Draft security checklist for air-gapped model import + KMS integration. Include export control/license checklist for model binaries. Due: 2025-11-12.
4) (Millbrook) Jonas to share 24h telemetry sample and a short doc describing peak burst characteristics (due 2025-11-07).
5) Schedule follow-up tech workshop (1.5h): deep dive on quantization tradeoffs and rollback strategy. Proposed week of 2025-11-17.

Technical notes / ideas to try in POC:
- Use a warm-standby pool: keep one instance with preloaded KV cache for each critical line to avoid cold-start tail.
- Dynamic model routing: route to quantized 13B normally, fallback to 7B quant when GPU memory fragmentation prevents allocation.
- Prefix caching: their sensor prompts have highly repetitive prefixes -> recommend prefix-level caching to reduce per-token compute.
- Lightweight local aggregator: batch small requests at the edge gateway for micro-batching (latency budget 5–10ms extra allowed) to amortize kernel launch.

Notes to self (Priya):
- Don't overpromise p99 until we test with their traces. Emphasize fallback policies and SLOs for degraded mode.
- Coordinate legal for model transfer paperwork early; air-gap procurement can add 4–6 weeks.
- Talk to runtime team about persistent KV cache work; tag as potential product improvement if many customers ask.

Reference links shared on call: (added to linked_artifacts above)

Quick log of informal follow-ups: 
- 2025-11-04: Sent onboarding checklist + SAS token instructions for secure upload.
- 2025-11-06: Jonas uploaded 6h sample (s3://millbrook-samples/lineA/6h.tar.gz) — need extraction + anonymization step.

Priority: high (POC -> Q1 internal pilot if POC shows <1.2x false-positive delta and p99 latency target met)
